t: netty-incubator-codec-ohttp: BinaryHttpParser should enforce limits for variable lengths fields
d: netty-incubator-codec-ohttp implements Oblivious HTTP (OHTTP) gateway and client functionality using Netty. Prior to 0.0.23.Final, BinaryHttpParser does not enforce limits on encoded variable-length fields controlled by a remote peer. A remote peer can cause the decoder to buffer data indefinitely until memory is exhausted, causing denial of service. This issue is fixed in version 0.0.23.Final.

t: Apache Tomcat: RewriteValve [F]/[G]/[R] rule matches do not stop processing
d: Execution After Redirect (EAR) vulnerability in Apache Tomcat in RedirectValve affecting flags [F], [G] and [R]. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M18 through 11.0.27, from 10.1.20 through 10.1.61, from 9.0.87 through 9.0.123. The following versions were EOL at the time the CVE was created but are known to be affected: 8.5.100. Other unsupported versions may also be affected. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.29, 10.1.62, 9.0.124, which fixes the issue. Note: Tomcat 11.0.28 was not released

t: netty-incubator-codec-ohttp: Binary HTTP parser infinite loop on known-length field section boundary
d: netty-incubator-codec-ohttp implements Oblivious HTTP (OHTTP) gateway and client functionality using Netty. Prior to 0.0.23.Final, BinaryHttpParser.readFieldLine in codec-bhttp/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/bhttp/BinaryHttpParser.java treats a complete field line that ends exactly at a known field-section boundary as incomplete and returns without consuming bytes. BinaryHttpParser.readFieldSection then leaves fieldSectionLength unchanged and repeats the loop because its forward-progress checks are Java assertions, which are normally disabled in production. A remote peer that sends a known-length Binary HTTP header or trailer section ending at that boundary can make the parser spin indefinitely and pin the Netty event-loop or worker thread responsible for the channel. This issue is fixed in version 0.0.23.Final.

t: Apache Tomcat: Fix for CVE-2026-25854 was incomplete
d: The fix for CVE-2026-25854 was incomplete. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.19 through 11.0.27, from 10.1.53 through 10.1.61, from 9.0.116 through 9.0.123. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.29, 10.1.62 or 9.0.124, which fix the issue. Note: Tomcat 11.0.28 was not released

t: netty-incubator-codec-ohttp: BoringSSL HPKE private key bytes exposed through toString() and exception messages
d: netty-incubator-codec-ohttp implements Oblivious HTTP (OHTTP) gateway and client functionality using Netty. Prior to 0.0.23.Final, BoringSSLAsymmetricCipherKeyPair.toString in codec-ohttp-hpke-classes-boringssl/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/hpke/boringssl/BoringSSLAsymmetricCipherKeyPair.java includes its private parameter, BoringSSLAsymmetricKeyParameter.toString in codec-ohttp-hpke-classes-boringssl/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/hpke/boringssl/BoringSSLAsymmetricKeyParameter.java renders the complete private-key byte array when isPrivate is true, and BoringSSL.EVP_HPKE_KEY_init_or_throw in codec-ohttp-hpke-classes-boringssl/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/hpke/boringssl/BoringSSL.java includes rejected privateKeyBytes in an exception message. Applications that log affected key-pair objects or initialization exceptions can persist complete HPKE private key material in logs or telemetry. Anyone who can read those records can recover the key and may compromise OHTTP message confidentiality or authenticity expectations while the key remains usable. This issue is fixed in version 0.0.23.Final.

In Dolibarr before 24.0.3, dolForgeSQLCriteriaCallback() in htdocs/core/lib/functions.lib.php allows account takeover because it strips only a single table-name prefix from a Universal Search Filter (sqlfilters) operand before checking it against the forbidden-field denylist (pass, pass_crypted, api_key). MariaDB and MySQL accept a two-level qualification such as schema.alias.column, so an operand of the form dolibarr.u.pass_crypted survives the check and is emitted into the WHERE clause. A remote authenticated user holding only the holiday read and readall permissions, which confer no user-management or administrative access, can use the resulting boolean oracle at GET /api/index.php/holidays to recover any user's bcrypt password hash and api_key one character at a time, including an administrator's. Because api_key is accepted directly by the REST API as a bearer credential, this yields full administrative control of the application. This bypasses the fix for CVE-2026-89012, which added only a strtolower() call and did not address prefix depth. The same denylist also omits pass_temp, which stores a password in cleartext, as well as national_registration_number, salary, birth, address, personal_mobile and note_private.

t: Apache Tomcat: HTTP/2 checks frame type before size leads to DoS
d: Missing release of resource after effective lifetime vulnerability in Apache Tomcat's HTTP/2 initial connection handling leads to DoS. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.27, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.61, from 9.0.20 through 9.0.123. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.29, 10.1.62 or 9.0.124, which fix the issue. Note: Tomcat 11.0.28 was not released

t: netty-incubator-codec-ohttp: Binary HTTP parser unchecked varint length overflow causes decoder crash
d: netty-incubator-codec-ohttp implements Oblivious HTTP (OHTTP) gateway and client functionality using Netty. Prior to 0.0.23.Final, BinaryHttpParser in codec-bhttp/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/bhttp/BinaryHttpParser.java accumulates attacker-controlled Binary HTTP variable-length integers into the int offset sumBytes. BinaryHttpParser.readRequestHead, BinaryHttpParser.readFieldLine, and BinaryHttpParser.getIndeterminateLength can narrow long lengths into that offset, causing integer wraparound before buffer indices are calculated. A remote peer that supplies a valid large encoded length to BinaryHttpParser or BinaryHttpDecoder can trigger an unchecked bounds exception from a small malformed message, fail or close the channel, and repeatedly cause denial of service. Java and Netty bounds checks prevent memory corruption, and no information disclosure was observed. This issue is fixed in version 0.0.23.Final.

t: Apache Tomcat: Memory leak with OWB integration leads to DoS
d: Missing release of memory after effective lifetime vulnerability in Apache Tomcat via WebSocket. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.27, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.61, from 9.0.22 through 9.0.123 The following versions were EOL at the time the CVE was created but are known to be affected: from 8.5.0 through 8.5.100, from 7.0.43 through 7.0.109. Other unsupported versions may also be affected. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.29, 10.0.62 or 9.0.124, which fix the issue. Note: Tomcat 11.0.28 was not released

t: Apache Tomcat: Jakarta Authentication secureResponse AuthException sends unprotected HTTP 200 response
d: Improper cleanup on thrown exception vulnerability in Apache Tomcat meant that an HTTP 200 response was sent rather than an HTTP 500 response after a AuthException was thrown during Jakarta Authentication secureResponse(). This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.27, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.61, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.123. The following versions were EOL at the time the CVE was created but are known to be affected: from 8.5.0 through 8.5.100. Other unsupported versions may also be affected. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.29, 10.0.62 or 9.0.124, which fix the issue. Note: Tomcat 11.0.28 was not released

t: Apache Tomcat: Incorrect security-role-ref with RequestDispatcher.forward()
d: Incorrect Authorization vulnerability in Apache Tomcat could occur during a request dispatch if the request depended on a security-role-ref provided by the dispatch target. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.27, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.61, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.123. The following versions were EOL at the time the CVE was created but are known to be affected: from 8.5.0 through 8.5.100, from 7.0.0 through 7.0.109. Other unsupported versions may also be affected. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.29, 10.1.62 or 9.0.124, which fixes the issue. Note: Tomcat 11.0.28 was not released

t: Apache Tomcat: Multiple vulnerabilities in EncryptInterceptor
d: Reliance on obfuscation or encryption of Security-Relevant inputs without integrity checking, Improper validation of integrity check value, Cleartext transmission of sensitive information vulnerability in the EncryptInterceptor of Apache Tomcat. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.27, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.61, from 9.0.13 through 9.0.123. The following versions were EOL at the time the CVE was created but are known to be affected: from 8.5.38 through 8.5.100, from 7.0.100 through 7.0.109. Other unsupported versions may also be affected. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.29, 10.1.62 or 9.0.124 and switch to TLS-PSK to encrypt cluster communication, which fixes the issue. Note: Tomcat 11.0.28 was not released

t: OSGeo shapelib dbfopen.c DBFCloneEmpty null pointer dereference
d: A weakness has been identified in OSGeo shapelib up to 1.6.3. This vulnerability affects the function DBFCloneEmpty of the file dbfopen.c. This manipulation causes null pointer dereference. It is possible to launch the attack on the local host. Patch name: f79050a900d2a05529501b2b714b8f89067db071. It is recommended to apply a patch to fix this issue.

t: IBM API Connect Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key
d: IBM API Connect 10.0.8.0 through 10.0.8.13 could allow a remote authenticated attacker to delete API keys belonging to other users due to improper authorization checks.

t: Multiple Vulnerabilities in watsonx.data
d: IBM watsonx.data 2.4.0 through 2.4.0 patch 8 does not invalidate session after a logout which could allow an authenticated user to impersonate another user on the system.

t: API Authentication and Rule Generation in the Auth0 Authorization Extension
d: In the Auth0 Authorization Extension, request authentication handling can process claims from query parameters independently of header validation. Under specific preconditions, this may allow an authenticated tenant user to issue requests to the extension's administrative endpoints. Also, input handling during rule generation may permit modification of the tenant login rule published by the extension.

t: Multiple Vulnerabilities in watsonx.data
d: IBM watsonx.data 2.4.0 through 2.4.0 patch 8 could allow unauthorized network access due to insufficient network segmentation controls.

t: Multiple Vulnerabilities in watsonx.data
d: IBM watsonx.data 2.4.0 through 2.4.0 patch 8 could allow a remote attacker to obtain sensitive information due to improper access control.

t: Multiple Vulnerabilities in watsonx.data
d: IBM watsonx.data 2.4.0 through 2.4.0 patch 8 could allow a local attacker to obtain sensitive credentials due to the use of a hard-coded cryptographic key.

t: Multiple Vulnerabilities in watsonx.data
d: IBM watsonx.data 2.4.0 through 2.4.0 patch 8 could allow a remote authenticated attacker to cause a denial of service due to client-side enforcement of business rules.

t: Multiple Vulnerabilities in watsonx.data
d: IBM watsonx.data 2.4.0 through 2.4.0 patch 8 could allow a remote authenticated attacker to conduct a server-side request forgery due to a server-side request forgery (SSRF) vulnerability.

t: Improper Request URL Validation in the Okta .NET SDK Abstractions Library
d: In the Okta .NET SDK Abstractions library, outbound HTTP requests are not restricted to the configured Okta organization domain when processing certain URL formats. If a URL parameter is modified to specify an external host, the library may transmit the configured SSWS API token to that unintended destination.

t: Path Parameter Encoding in Okta Swift Management SDK
d: The Okta Swift Management SDK does not percent-encode forward slash (/) characters during path parameter interpolation. If an application supplies input containing relative path sequences (e.g., ../) to an SDK method, standard URL normalization may direct the outbound request to an alternative Okta Management API endpoint.

t: Improper Synchronization in the Okta .NET SDK Abstractions Library
d: The Okta .NET SDK Abstractions library improperly synchronizes authentication credentials set on a shared HTTP client during request execution. When concurrent requests are dispatched for different principals, one principal's credential may be transmitted on an outbound request intended for another principal, which can result in credential exposure and lead to unauthorized actions performed as the affected principal at the Okta Management API.

t: Credential Overwriting in Okta .NET SDK Abstractions Library
d: The Okta .NET SDK Abstractions library systematically writes per-request authentication credentials to a shared HTTP client instance, rather than being isolated to individual outbound request objects. When using scoped child clients, a subsequent scoped request can overwrite the shared client configuration. Because the original parent client credential has not been restored, subsequent outbound requests may be transmitted using the newly written credential, which can result in subsequent actions being executed under the context of an incorrect security principal in the Okta Management API and improper attribution in audit logs.

t: Front-Channel Parameter Handling in Okta Client SDK for Python
d: The Okta Client SDK for Python (okta-client-python) includes client authentication values (client_secret or JWT assertions) as query parameters in the front-channel authorization URL when executing the authorization code flow without Pushed Authorization Requests (PAR). When PAR is disabled, unsupported by the authorization server, or fails, the SDK falls back to standard authorization URL construction, transmitting these parameters via user-agent requests.

t: FreeRDP Smartcard Redirection Memory Handling in Okta Privileged Access Gateway
d: Okta Privileged Access (OPA) Gateway includes a version of the FreeRDP library affected by memory management issues in its smartcard redirection handling. When an RDP session is established meeting specific session criteria, command execution within the context of the local Gateway service account may be allowed.

t: Symbolic Link Resolution in Okta Verify for macOS
d: On Intel-based macOS systems, the Okta Device Access (ODA) component of Okta Verify for macOS configures a LaunchDaemon service whose program path resolves via a symbolic link in /usr/local/bin. In environments where non-standard directory permissions grant local non-root users write access to this path, the symbolic link target can be modified, causing the LaunchDaemon to execute the replacement binary upon service restart.

t: IBM Guardium Data Protection Missing Authentication
d: IBM Guardium Data Protection 12.2 is vulnerable to missing authentication in the SharePoint S-TAP RelayService, allowing an unauthenticated network attacker to inject forged audit events and access the active monitoring policy.

t: GCM authentication tag length downgrade in Amazon S3 Encryption Client for PHP
d: Insufficient verification of data authenticity in the decryption component of Amazon S3 Encryption Client for PHP in AWS SDK for PHP before 3.383.1 might allow an authenticated remote user to forge ciphertext that decrypts to arbitrary plaintext via manipulation of the GCM authentication tag length metadata. To remediate this issue, users should upgrade to AWS SDK for PHP version 3.383.1 or later.

t: IBM Guardium Data Protection Buffer Overflow
d: IBM Guardium Data Protection 12.2 is vulnerable to a stack-based buffer overflow when processing a specially crafted PROXY protocol v1 header. A remote attacker can exploit this vulnerability to cause a denial of service or potentially execute arbitrary code.

t: IBM Guardium Data Protection Out-of-bounds Read
d: IBM Guardium Data Protection 12.2 could allow a remote attacker to obtain sensitive information or cause a denial of service due to an out-of-bounds heap read.

t: IBM Guardium Data Protection Improper Privilege Management
d: IBM Guardium Data Protection 12.2 is vulnerable to local privilege escalation via the SUID-root podman_wrapper binary on the Collector appliance. A local attacker with low-privileged access to the Collector can exploit insufficient argument validation in the SUID binary to execute arbitrary commands as root, resulting in full compromise of the Collector appliance.

t: IBM Guardium Data Protection Improper Output Neutralization for Logs
d: IBM Guardium Data Protection 12.2 could allow a remote attacker to inject forged audit records due to improper output neutralization for logs.

t: IBM Guardium Data Protection Deserialization of Untrusted Data
d: IBM Guardium Data Protection 12.2 is vulnerable to insecure deserialization in the SharePoint Tap MulticastTransceiver component. An unauthenticated remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability to execute arbitrary code on the affected system.

t: IBM Guardium Data Protection Path Traversal
d: IBM Guardium Data Protection 12.2 is vulnerable to path traversal in the datasource functionality. An authenticated attacker could exploit this vulnerability to delete arbitrary files on the appliance.

t: IBM Guardium Data Protection Improper Certificate Validation
d: IBM Guardium Data Protection 12.2 is vulnerable to improper TLS certificate validation in the GDP Terraform provider, allowing a network attacker with a man-in-the-middle position to intercept sensitive credentials transmitted to the Guardium appliance.

t: IBM Guardium Data Protection SQL Injection
d: IBM Guardium Data Protection 12.2 is vulnerable to SQL injection in the edge-controller component. An unauthenticated remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability to access or modify sensitive database information.
